slides.title: Introduction to Loops
slides.content: Loops repeat code multiple times. The for loop is used when you know how many times to iterate.

exercise.prompt: When is a for loop most appropriate?

slides.title: For Loop Syntax
slides.content: A for loop has three parts: initialization, condition, and iteration. The loop continues while the condition is true.

slides.title: Counting Down
slides.content: You can count backwards by starting high and decrementing. Use i-- to decrease the counter.

exercise.prompt: Complete the loop to count from 10 down to 5

slides.title: Foreach Loop
slides.content: The foreach loop iterates over every element in a collection. You cannot modify the collection during iteration.

slides.title: Loop Control
slides.content: Inside a loop, break exits immediately. Continue skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next.

exercise.prompt: Choose the correct control statement to skip an iteration

slides.title: Nested Loops
slides.content: You can place loops inside other loops. The inner loop completes all iterations for each outer loop iteration.

exercise.prompt: A loop inside another loop is called a _____ loop

slides.title: Loop Variables Scope
slides.content: Variables declared in the for loop initialization exist only within the loop. They cannot be accessed outside.

exercise.prompt: Where is the loop variable accessible?

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content: Use meaningful variable names. Avoid infinite loops by ensuring the condition eventually becomes false. Prefer foreach for simple collection iteration.

exercise.prompt: Select the best loop for iterating all elements

slides.title: Flow Builder: For Loop
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to create a for loop that counts from 1 to 3.

exercise.prompt: Build a flow with a for loop from 1 to 3 that outputs the counter
